item.title: Central North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ACPN50 PHFO 261132
TWOCP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 AM HST Wed Aug 26 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located several hundred miles north of Kure Atoll, and
on Tropical Storm Iselle, located well to the west of the southern
tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

Western East Pacific:
An elongated, broad area of low pressure located well to the
east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands is producing disorganized
showers and thunderstorms. Environmental conditions appear conducive
for gradual development of this system, and a tropical depression is
likely to form late this week or early this weekend while the system
drifts to the northeast, then turns westward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...40 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well south of the Hawaiian
Islands late this week or over the weekend. Some gradual development
is possible by early next week while the system moves slowly
west-northwestward, well south-southwest of the Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Kelly
NNNN

item.description:

BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Lala Advisory Number  57
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM HST Wed Aug 26 2026
 
...LALA EXPECTED TO BECOME A REMNANT LOW IN A COUPLE OF DAYS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 AM HST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...35.8N 178.0W
ABOUT 585 MI...945 KM NNW OF PEARL AND HERMES ATOLL
ABOUT 510 MI...825 KM N OF KURE ATOLL
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNW OR 330 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...997 MB...29.44 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 AM HST (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Lala was
located near latitude 35.8 North, longitude 178.0 West. Lala is
moving toward the north-northwest near 5 mph (7 km/h) and a slow 
north-northwestward to northwestward motion is expected over the 
next couple of days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 45 mph (75 km/h) with higher gusts.
Gradual weakening is expected during the next couple of days, and
Lala is forecast to become a post-tropical remnant low by late 
Thursday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 115 miles (185 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 997 mb (29.44 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Pasch

item.title: Tropical Storm Lala Forecast Discussion Number 57
item.description:
Issued at 500 AM HST Wed Aug 26 2026 
068 
WTPA42 PHFO 261437
TCDCP2
 
Tropical Storm Lala Discussion Number  57
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM HST Wed Aug 26 2026
 
Lala's deep convection has been decreasing in coverage, with 
continued evidence of dry air intrusion over the southern portion of 
the circulation.  Also, some southwesterly vertical wind shear 
appears to now be affecting the system.  Although Dvorak intensity 
estimates are slowly decreasing, a Metop-C scatterometer pass from a 
few hours ago suggests that the intensity is still near 40 kt.  The 
SHIPS guidance shows increasing shear over Lala with relatively dry 
air, and SSTs should remain near 23 deg C.  Therefore, additional 
slow weakening is likely and Lala is expected to degenerate into a 
post-tropical remnant low in 48 hours.  The system is forecast to 
cross the International Date line around that time as well.

Recent center fixes now show a slow north-northwestward motion 
around 330/4 kt.  A mid-level ridge to the northeast of Lala should 
result in a north-northwesterly to northwesterly track for the next 
few days.  The official track prediction is only a tad to the right 
and slightly slower than the previous NHC forecast.  This is in 
close agreement with the latest corrected consensus, HCCA, guidance. 
 Post-tropical Lala is forecast to accelerate deeper into the 
mid-latitudes over the weekend, and it should open up into a trough 
over the northern Pacific before reaching the western Aleutian 
Islands.
